pioneer-wave-1b1-task-11: `declare -A CATEGORY_SIZE` needs bash 4, absent from macOS's system bash 3.2; replaced with a parallel indexed array aligned to the existing `categories` array (trivial substitution, keys were already an ordered indexed array). Also fixed `((line_count++))`/`((issue_count++))` aborting the whole script under `set -e` the first time each counter left 0 (post-increment evaluates to the old, zero, value) — pre-existing, found while proving this script runs at all. Also moved an inline `[[ =~ ]]` regex with parenthesised groups into a variable: unpatched bash 3.2 hard-fails to parse the literal form ("syntax error in conditional expression"), found by actually running this script under a compiled bash 3.2 for Step 4.

pioneer-wave-1b1-task-11: `declare -A KNOWN_GUIDS` needs bash 4; it was a set (value always 1) used only for membership tests against every .meta file in the project, so a newline-table-plus-grep-per-lookup substitution would turn an O(1) test into O(n) per lookup and the whole pass into O(n*m) on a real project's tens of thousands of .meta files. Replaced with a sorted, deduplicated indexed array (KNOWN_GUIDS_SORTED) built once and a binary search (guid_known(), O(log n) per lookup). Also replaced two `grep -oP ... \K` extractions (GNU-only PCRE, one of them piped into `head -1`, a reader that can exit before its writer finishes) with `sed`, and fixed six `((var++))` counters that aborted the script under `set -e` the first time each left 0 — pre-existing, found while proving this script runs at all.

pioneer-wave-1b1-task-11: seven `declare -A` maps needed bash 4. Six were keyed on assembly name (ASMDEF_NAME_TO_PATH, ASMDEF_REFS, ASMDEF_DIR, ASMDEF_IS_EDITOR, ASMDEF_IS_TEST, ASMDEF_TEST_ONLY) and became one set of parallel indexed arrays, one record per assembly (ASMDEF_NAME_TO_PATH's reverse, ASMDEF_PATH_TO_NAME, was dead code — written, never read — and was not resurrected). Name->index lookups use a linear scan (assembly counts don't reach the scale that would need better than O(n); assembly names contain dots, illegal in bash identifiers, ruling out a `printf -v`-sanitised-name scheme without its own collision handling). VISIT_STATE (the DFS cycle-detector's mutable 0/1/2 state, keyed the same way) is a parallel indexed array for the same O(1)-per-write reason. Verified against fixtures with a known 3-cycle (still reported), a duplicate assembly name (still reported), a genuine Editor/Runtime violation (still reported), and a clean 2-assembly graph (no false positives). Also fixed four `((var++))` counters that aborted the script under `set -e` the first time each left 0 — pre-existing, found while proving this script runs at all.

pioneer-wave-1b1-task-11: `declare -A COUNTS` needs bash 4; replaced with a parallel indexed array aligned to the existing `CATEGORIES` array plus a category_index() lookup (trivial substitution, keys were already an ordered indexed array). Also replaced `head -n "$target_line" "$file" | tac | head -n 100` — the second `head` can exit before `tac` finishes writing once target_line exceeds 100, and under `set -euo pipefail` that SIGPIPE aborts the whole script — with a single awk pass over the file. Also fixed `((total_issues++))`/`((file_count++))` aborting the script under `set -e` the first time each counter left 0 (pre-existing; this meant the script could never complete a single scan before this fix — found while proving it runs at all for Step 4).

pioneer-wave-1b1-task-11: `declare -A guid_map` (guid -> path, unbounded) needs bash 4; a real Unity project has tens of thousands of .meta files, so a naive newline-table-plus-grep-per-file substitution would turn an O(1) hash test into O(n) per file and O(n^2) overall. Replaced with a single sorted pass: collect "guid<TAB>path" once per .meta file, sort once (O(n log n), stable so first-seen ordering survives), walk once (O(n)) comparing each entry only to its immediate neighbor (duplicates are adjacent after sorting on the guid field). Also replaced `grep -oP` (GNU-only PCRE) with `sed`, and fixed two `((var++))` counters that aborted the script under `set -e` the first time each left 0 — pre-existing (confirmed by running the unmodified script against a fixture: it silently stopped after the very first reported error), found while proving this script runs at all.

pioneer-wave-1b1-task-9: lines 165 and 167 piped a whole file's content (NEW_FIELDS, and NEW_CONTENT which is the entire scanned C# file) into `grep -q`/`grep -qx`; NEW_CONTENT in particular can exceed PIPE_BUF, letting grep exit before the writer finishes and SIGPIPE it under set -euo pipefail (the early-exit-pipe shape from Task 7). Replaced both with here-strings.

test-runner-fix: sourced files ended in exit, killing the runner after file 1; --source-only was unimplemented; dynamic test source is intentional. Concurrent full-suite runs supplied enough scheduling pressure to trigger it. Fixed by replacing the pipe with a here-string, which has no live writer process to SIGPIPE.
